title: F. Firefly's Queries
statement:
Firefly is given an array a of length n. Let c_i denote the i'th cyclic shift^{∗} of a. She creates a new array b such that b = c_1 + c_2 + … + c_n where + represents concatenation^{†}.

Then, she asks you q queries. For each query, output the sum of all elements in the subarray of b that starts from the l-th element and ends at the r-th element, inclusive of both ends.

^{∗}The x-th (1 ≤ x ≤ n) cyclic shift of the array a is a_x, a_{x+1} … a_n, a_1, a_2 … a_{x - 1}. Note that the 1-st shift is the initial a.

^{†}The concatenation of two arrays p and q of length n (in other words, p + q) is p_1, p_2, ..., p_n, q_1, q_2, ..., q_n.

The first line contains t (1 ≤ t ≤ 10^4) — the number of test cases.

The first line of each test case contains two integers n and q (1 ≤ n, q ≤ 2·10^5) — the length of the array and the number of queries.

The following line contains n integers a_1, a_2, ..., a_n (1 ≤ a_i ≤ 10^6).

The following q lines contain two integers l and r (1 ≤ l ≤ r ≤ n^2) — the left and right bounds of the query.

Note that the large inputs may require the use of 64-bit integers.

It is guaranteed that the sum of n does not exceed 2·10^5 and the sum of q does not exceed 2·10^5.

For each query, output the answer on a new line.

For the first test case, b = [1, 2, 3, 2, 3, 1, 3, 1, 2].

Input:
```
53 31 2 31 93 58 85 54 8 3 2 41 143 77 102 111 251 161 15 73 1 6 10 43 216 172 21 51 149 1512 135 34 9 10 10 120 253 1120 22
```

Output:
```
18
8
1
55
20
13
41
105
6
96
62
1
24
71
31
14
44
65
15
```
